text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] org spike detected for org=helios-inc (org_id: org_8962). Sustained QPS spike + elevated 5xxs. 95p latency ~1.8s. Paging on-call: @alice_sre. Dash: https://grafana.redwood/boards/helios-inc-spike · incident: INC-2026-045

alice_sre: Acked. I'm here — pulling RL and quota tables for org_8962 now. Do we know which route/model is hot (gpt-open-16k vs gpt-embed-4k)?

ben_oncall: I'm oncall and jumping in. Looks like most of the traffic is generation requests against `gpt-open-16k` with heavy reranking calls appended (semantic-rerank). Token/sec per session spiked 4x.

alice_sre: Proposal: temporary emergency adjustments — 1) bump org token cap from 1500/min -> 3000/min for 60m; 2) relax concurrency cap from 4 -> 8; 3) disable semantic-rerank feature for this org to stop expensive downstream calls. Want a quick customer check before we flip anything?

mara_support: I'm reaching out to Helios now (support channel + phone). Will confirm tolerance for degraded ranking. ETA 3m.

katie_prod: From product: ok to proceed with emergency mitigations if oncall confirms safety and infra approves. Need explicit rollback window and communication step.

ben_oncall: Executing manual override now. CLI run:
```
redwoodctl org update-quota --org org_8962 --token-rate 3000 --duration 60m --reason "emergency-qps-mitigation"
redwoodctl org update-concurrency --org org_8962 --concurrency 8 --duration 60m
```
Will apply feature flag after quotas are in place.

incident-bot: [AUDIT] quota/concurrency change applied by ben_oncall. change_id=chg_7892 · run_id=run_3321

dave_infra: Heads-up: hosted pool us-east is showing GPU saturation. I'll initiate short-term routing of helios traffic to reserved pool `dedicated-012` (capacity available) to protect other tenants. Kicking off routing change.

alice_sre: Also applying feature flag:
```
ffctl set helio_semantic_rerank org_8962 false --env prod --note "mitigate token spike"
```
Putting this behind a guarded rollout to avoid config storms.

mara_support: Helios on the line: they're seeing slower but acceptable results; they asked for a 1-hour window and to be notified before revert. They've accepted temporary reduction in rerank quality.

ben_oncall: Monitoring metrics now — 5xxs down 60% in last 5m, p95 latency reduced to ~900ms. Live: https://grafana.redwood/boards/helios-inc-spike (watch token/sec and error-rate panels).

katie_prod: Good. Rollback plan: after 60m, revert token-rate and concurrency to previous values and re-enable rerank unless new anomalies. Assign owner to confirm before revert — @jordan_acct to handle customer notice and @alice_sre to validate metrics pre/post.

jordan_acct: I will draft a short note with timeline and estimated billing impact for the temporary bump. Logging action for billing: BILL-LOG-3344.

incident-bot: [UPDATE] routing change succeeded — helios -> dedicated-012. audit_id=rout_558

ben_oncall: Metrics stable for 18m. Error-rate trending to baseline. Leaving the emergency overrides active until the 60m timer expires, then we'll perform the controlled rollback.

alice_sre: Post-incident item: investigate why rerank calls multiplied tokens (likely duplicated prompts + missing caching). Assign eng-ml. PI ticket PI-4567 created.

mara_support: Helios confirmed they received comms and are okay. They requested a quick postmortem and an estimate for crediting them for the degraded quality window.

katie_prod: Thank you team. Please capture all CLI commands and audit IDs in the incident ticket. After rollback, create a short blameless postmortem and recommended preventative controls (auto-disable rerank under token spike, rate-based feature circuit).

incident-bot: [RESOLVE] Incident INC-2026-045 mitigated and closed to monitoring. Actions taken: emergency token cap bump (1500->3000) for 60m, concurrency relax (4->8), feature flag `helio_semantic_rerank=false`, routed traffic to dedicated-012. audit_ids: chg_7892, rout_558. Post-incident: PI-4567 assigned. :white_check_mark:

alice_sre: Leaving oncall notes and handoff to next rotation. If anything regresses reopen with the incident ID. Closing thread. :lock:
